name: Document: Reconcile the two canon artifacts into one version of record
text_content:
sources/brand-guidelines.md (Version 1.0) and sources/brand-guidelines-deck.pdf (Version 3.0) have drifted from each other on the six-tier authority hierarchy, on the presence of "the order is the decision," and on the chef seat's terminology. Canon's own rule is that a living document "changes by versioned decision, never by drift," so the drift is a violation of canon by canon.

The work: name one artifact the canon of record and the other a rendering of it; apply the tier ruling from 86akh3rx4; scope the authority claim "the source of truth for every decision made under this name" to what canon actually governs; and state canon's relationship to the operating charter in the same words the charter uses.

Follows the hierarchy ruling. Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in sections 3 and 4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 13 found that "No exploitation ever" is defined in neither canon artifact, as Session 12 found "toxicity" undefined, and that the compensation architecture is the instrument by which the non-negotiable is honored or breached: the line between a training weight, a closed-day pay rule, or a payment rhythm that is lean and one that is exploitation is undrawn. comment.text: Session 12 adds two items to the reconciliation and one to the hierarchy ruling. Deck 3.0 states both edges of the Playground ("Rules so tight the result is foreclosed" and "Openness so loose the space stops feeling safe," p.14) while Canon 1.0 states only the foreclosure test; whether a house can fail by not correcting at all, the forgot-to coach as a canon violation, is stated in one version only, and Session 12 reads both edges as binding (finding 18.12). Canon's Nunchi, "not diagnostic inquiry," sits against the record's "diagnostic" and against coaching by hypothesis as an act, not only as a word (finding 18.4). And for the hierarchy ruling: "No toxicity ever" is at Tier 2 in the deck and unranked in the text, and neither artifact defines toxicity, so the line between hard feedback and the thing the non-negotiable forbids is undrawn (finding 18.9); the founders with canon's owner should draw it beside the tier ruling. S12 page, section 18; findings 18.4, 18.9, 18.12.

Session 8 (Team structures), 2026-09-13. Extended.

Session 8 adds to the reconciliation: under Brandon's ruling on
86akh5u9g

, canon's "floor manager" (Canon 1.0 section 08; Deck 3.0 pp. 79 and 81) and "Maître d'" (Canon 1.0 section 06; Deck 3.0 pp. 68 and 81) are one seat, and the floor manager role leaves both uniform tables and the service model's floor-authority paragraph. Two consequences: the sonic tiers "management sign-off" and "floor management" (Canon 1.0 section 07; Deck 3.0 p.75) assume two management strata on the floor and now face one seat (S8 finding 21.2); and canon's Maître d' at the top of the porch steps and seating every table (Canon 1.0 sections 06 and 08) is read by the team as a register set by whoever holds the door that service, not a fixed post, because a room owner walking every table is a room no one is reading (S8 finding 21.1, P5, founder-gated with canon's owner). Canon's form "Maître d'" governs any surface a customer or candidate reads.
